Subject: Data retention / backup purge question — possible short extension

Hi Kimberly,

Quick note from our Security & Ops team — during our platform migration (scheduled for next week) we need to request a short hold on the automatic backup purge for two log buckets that contain a subset of patient metadata and request a temporary TTL rollback for recent logs (roughly 30 days beyond the current TTL) while we confirm a safe re-ingest path.

Can Redwood provide: 1) a concrete timeline for how long we can keep expired backups in a quarantined state before purge, 2) confirmation about whether a temporary TTL rollback is feasible without long-term policy changes, and 3) a statement on whether any subprocessor re-encryption / copy would be performed during the hold?

We've attached our annotated DPA questions to highlight the specific clauses we need to align. This is time-sensitive — procurement needs a short written proposal and proposed amendment so we can sign off.

Thanks,
Alice Barker
Head of Security Programs
BlueCrest Health

Karthik — can you confirm storage/ops impact and whether we need a snapshot restore path to satisfy BlueCrest's re-ingest requirement?

Alice — if the scope above looks right, I will circulate a short amendment and a technical runbook (for procurement and your audit team) within 48 hours.

Kimberly / Alice — technical readout below.

On Wed, Sep 10, 2025 at 10:00 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> High-level proposal (quick):
> - Scope: two named log buckets (please confirm bucket IDs) and associated nightly backups created between 2025-08-01 and 2025-09-08.

Confirmed scope (please validate IDs):
- s3://bluecrest-logs/prod-events-2025 and s3://bluecrest-logs/audit-events-2025
- Estimated size: 1.2 TB combined; current lifecycle policy set to delete objects older than 60 days.

Operational plan options:
1) Quarantine prefix + pause purge job (low risk): we copy objects to s3://redwood-temp-quarantine/bluecrest/YYYYMMDD and add a metadata tag retain=bluecrest-ttl-hold. Purge job checks the tag and skips. Storage cost: approx $30/day.
2) TTL rollback (medium risk): modify object lifecycle to extend expiry by 30 days for keys matching timestamp range; faster but interacts with current lifecycle engine and requires careful rollback logic.
3) Snapshot + export (safe, higher cost): create immutable snapshots and provide an export package for BlueCrest to download.

Constraints / notes:
- Subprocessors: if we copy or export and any third-party transfer is performed (e.g., external archive provider), we must notify and get their attestations — current subprocessor list attached in the runbook.
- Auditability: ops will enable S3 server access logs and will produce an audit log of any copy/modify operations.
- Rollback mechanics: we can revert lifecycle changes within 24 hours if needed; however, re-encrypting or changing KMS wrappers requires 48–72 hours and coordination with our KMS provider.

Recommendation: option 1 (quarantine prefix + pause purge) for up to 30 days, with a one-time TTL extension for very recent keys if BlueCrest needs immediate access.

I'll draft the runbook and the storage-cost estimate and attach redwood-temporary-ttl-plan.xlsx.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice / Kimberly — legal follow-up.

On Thu, Sep 11, 2025 at 2:30 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Recommendation: option 1 (quarantine prefix + pause purge) for up to 30 days...

We can accommodate a time-boxed operational hold, but we need a short DPA addendum that:
- Specifies the exact objects/buckets under the exception,
- Limits the retention extension to a maximum of 30 calendar days from the agreed start date,
- Requires BlueCrest to confirm that the retained data will not be used to expand processing (i.e., only for migration/re-ingest),
- Requires audit access to Redwood's access logs for the hold period (read-only) and a confirmation that no subprocessors will export data off our controlled storage without prior written approval.

Proposed next steps: I have a draft amendment ready (minor edits) and will send a DocuSign link for procurement. The clause will include a requirement for an attestation from any third-party archive vendor if BlueCrest requests export.

I'll attach the proposed language and mark the change as a limited-scope addendum (amended-dpa-bluecrest.docx).

—Jonas Weber
Counsel, Redwood Inference

Alice — thanks for patience while we scoped this. Summary and agreed plan below.

Agreed scope:
- Buckets: s3://bluecrest-logs/prod-events-2025 and s3://bluecrest-logs/audit-events-2025 (confirmed)
- Timebox: Redwood will pause automated purge jobs and quarantine objects for 30 days starting 2025-09-17 through 2025-10-17.
- Technical: Ops will create a quarantine copy and tag objects retain=bluecrest-ttl-hold. We will not change KMS envelopes; no re-encryption will occur.
- Export: Any export request must be accompanied by an attestation for any subprocessors; exports require signed approval per the addendum.

Deliverables and next steps:

2) Karthik will publish the runbook and an estimated storage cost (approx $900 for 30 days) and enable S3 access logs for the period.
3) I will coordinate a short call for 2025-09-16 to confirm cutover steps and share a one-page summary for your audit team.
